references.text: The previous verse describes how Phinehas rose from the assembly, took a spear in his hand, leading directly to the action in verse 8.
The Lord's assessment of Phinehas' action, where he is praised for his zeal and receives a covenant of peace and an everlasting priesthood.
Identifies the names of the two who were killed: Zimri son of Salu, and Cozbi daughter of Zur.
Describes the result of the plague that was stopped, stating that 24,000 died.
Refers back to the incident at Peor where the plague struck the Lord's assembly.
The psalm describes the same event where Phinehas intervened and the plague was stopped, and this was credited to him as righteousness.
David stops a pestilence by building an altar, parallel to how Phinehas' action stopped the plague.
Reference to the sin at Peor as a warning to the children of Israel.
